messages:
alex_sales: Quick thread — Acme is ready to sign but procurement flagged a capacity-commitment clause on the price schedule. They want a 60-day termination-for-convenience window and an explicit burst-credit allowance. Any immediate objections?

siva_se: For Dedicated we can do a limited burst pool (3 months) without changing the MSA; it's an order-form addendum. Pricing team needs to ok the burst quantity.

jess_legal: High-level: 60-day TFC on committed capacity is risky — it undermines committed revenue. Recommend 90 days for committed pools, 30 days for hosted. We can document the differences on the order form.

maria_procure: Customer is pushing 60 days. They also want the DPA to list StorageX as a subprocessor and require EU residency for certain data. Do we have StorageX covered in our subprocessor registry?

alex_sales: StorageX was onboarded in Q2 and is in the registry. We can add them to the DPA addendum and include region pinning for EU on Private/Dedicated.

jess_legal: I'll prepare minimal redlines. Key asks from our side: remove unilateral 60-day termination on committed capacity, add mutual-TFC language and a pro-rata settlement clause, and add an infra subprocessor indemnity carveout.

alex_sales: Please paste the short clause we can give to procurement to speed this up.

jess_legal: Pasting suggested minimal language to insert into the order form addendum:

```
Section 3.2 (Committed Capacity Termination): Customer may terminate committed capacity with 90 days' written notice. Redwood may terminate for cause with 30 days' notice. If Customer terminates committed capacity prior to the end of the applicable term, Customer will be responsible for a pro-rata charge equal to the remaining committed months, which may be satisfied via invoice or account credit at Redwood's discretion.
```

siva_se: Ops note — if we accept pro-rata refunds applied as invoice credits, that's doable without touching billing code. If customer insists on cash refunds, billing will need a webhook/update; ETA ~2 weeks.

jess_legal: To avoid product changes, propose credit-only settlement; that's standard and keeps timelines short.

maria_procure: Customer requires esign flow with multiple signers, CC to legal@acme.com, and an explicit PO number field on the signature page. Can DocuSign support all three for the envelope?

alex_sales: Yes, DocuSign supports multiple signers + CC + custom fields. I'll assemble the envelope after we finalize redlines. Need redline packet link.

contracts-bot: automated note — order packet generated (id: OP-48293). Link: https://contracts.redwood.ai/packets/OP-48293

jess_legal: Redline uploaded to OP-48293 and annotated. Tagged @alex_sales for sending. Key annotation: change 'termination for convenience' timings + add StorageX to the subprocessor appendix.

alex_sales: Sending to customer now with cc to @maria_procure and legal@acme.com. I'll add PO field and the burst pool as an attachment. Will update thread if Acme pushes back on 90->60. :thumbsup:

maria_procure: Thanks — standing by for invoice and payment routing instructions.
